item.research_question: Can a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy be successfully fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) despite processing challenges, and how do its microstructure, hardness, and corrosion resistance compare to traditional superalloys and arc-melted counterparts?
item.material_system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal equiatomic composition of Nb, Mo, Ta, W powders with 99.9% purity)
item.processing_route: Selective laser melting (SLM) using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with a 500 W fiber laser in an argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen); parameters included hatch distance 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.1 mm, laser power factor 0.8, scanning velocity 250 mm/s, and a triple-pass remelting strategy (3x energy input) to achieve a linear energy density of 2.83 J/mm
item.test_conditions: Microstructure and composition analyzed via SEM and EDS; crystal structure via XRD (Cu target, λ = 1.54 Å); microhardness measured on XY plane; corrosion resistance evaluated via potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution (scanning range −0.2 V to +0.2 V) and high-voltage scanning (−1.5 to +2 V)
key_findings: A single BCC solid solution was formed with an experimental lattice parameter of 3.2034 Å, close to the theoretical 3.2230 Å.
Elements with lower melting points and densities (Nb and Mo) showed negative molar ratio deviations of up to 3.5% and 0.16%, respectively, while Ta showed a positive deviation of 28.21%.
The average grain size was 13.4 μm, significantly smaller than the 200 μm observed in as-cast NbMoTaW HEA.
Primary and secondary dendrite arm spacings were 6.59 μm and 1.68 μm, respectively, compared to 20–30 μm in as-cast samples.
The average microhardness of the SLM-fabricated sample was 826 Hv, compared to 446 Hv for the arc-melted counterpart and 310–437 Hv for superalloys.
The free-corrosion current density of the HEA was 8.716 × 10⁻¹¹ A, which is two orders of magnitude lower than that of 316 L steel (8.815 × 10⁻⁹ A).
Visual corrosion testing showed 316 L steel suffered up to 1 mm corrosion depth, whereas the HEA exhibited only crack extension and minor pitting.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the fine microstructure to the extremely high cooling rates and temperature gradients inherent to SLM, which limit growth time despite large driving forces. Composition deviations are explained by the combined effects of melting point, liquid density, particle size, and laser absorption: lower melting point elements fuse first and evaporate more, while lower density liquids float to the surface and absorb more energy, leading to negative deviations for Nb and Mo.
item.limitations: The text states that 'the ductility of the NbMoTaW HEA at room temperature is low' and that 'further study of mechanical properties is still necessary' to fully assess the material's potential.
item.future_work: The authors propose that 'further study of mechanical properties is still necessary' to validate the improvements in plasticity and fatigue strength suggested by the Hall–Petch law and grain refinement.
quotes: The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys
The average grain size is 13.4 μm, which is much smaller compared with the 200 μm of as-cast NbMoTaW HEA grain size
The free-corrosion current of the HEA is reduced by two orders of magnitude compared with that of the 316 L steel
